headline: The US health research agency ARPA-H has opened a new program called SURPASS to build faster, AI-supported clinical trials.
score_reason: Meaningful government program, but announced 30 Sep (older than 6 Oct) and still at the call-for-proposals stage; lowered by 1.
importance_line: Patients waiting for new treatments and drug developers could eventually see shorter trials, but SURPASS is only seeking proposals now and results are years away.
summary: The law firm Hogan Lovells reports that the US Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) launched a program called SURPASS on 30 Sep 2026, aiming to build long-running adaptive trials that combine AI prediction models, shared infrastructure and real-time data analysis to cut clinical trial timelines. Proposal summaries are due 30 Nov 2026, so the program is still at the stage of seeking ideas from industry.
notes: Read a law firm summary, not the ARPA-H notice itself; source credited accordingly.
